[LECC.4.3] The adapter names the leaf under `adapter`
(`adapter.throttled`), in [LECC.1.2]'s shape. The rule runs both ways. An
adapter must not stretch `request` or `internal` to cover something their
semantics do not: `request.*` is about the request as it crossed the DS
boundary and `internal.*` about a bug in the adapter or the runtime, so
any failure of the system the adapter fronts is neither and
belongs under `adapter.*`. Equally, an adapter must not
mint an `adapter.*` name for a condition `request` or `internal` already
covers — malformed arguments are `request.malformed`, not
`adapter.bad_args`. Two names for one condition is what
this rule exists to prevent.
